headline: High: shared local filesystem and overlapping write/git capabilities make Cursor↔GitHub Copilot prone to prompt injection, data leakage, and conflicting edits by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads/writes workspace files and clipboard contents, and its shared state with other instances is via local filesystem. GitHub Copilot reads repo context/open buffers and proposes edits. That creates a plausible file-based injection path, though not a direct raw-web parser. Both agents are exposed through the same workspace channel.
conditions: IF Cursor and Copilot operate on the same workspace files, injected instructions in a file can influence both agents.
IF Copilot Workspace or Cursor Agent consumes file text as instructions without provenance checks, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Separate the agents into different workspaces or clones.
Disable Cursor clipboard-based workflows for shared content.
Require manual review of any file containing model-generated instructions.
Use provenance tags or comments to mark untrusted text.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches open files, clipboard contents, and broad network egress to model providers/MCP servers; Copilot reads repo context and sends it to api.githubcopilot.com. If both see the same workspace, sensitive code or secrets can flow from shared files into two third-party backends. The pair is closed-source, so interaction details are only docs-based.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains secrets or regulated code, both agents can ingest it.
IF Cursor MCP or Copilot chat/workspace is enabled on that workspace, file contents may be transmitted off-host.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared repo/workspace.
Disable Copilot Chat/Workspace on sensitive folders.
Disable Cursor MCP servers for the shared project.
Use separate Git remotes or sanitized mirrors for agent work.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction before any outbound model call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands; Copilot Workspace can also apply edits and modify git state. Both have write access to the same repo context, and neither profile shows locking or coordination. Concurrent edits and git-state changes can overwrite each other or corrupt branches by default.
conditions: IF both agents are active on the same git checkout, simultaneous edits can conflict.
IF Cursor Yolo mode is enabled while Copilot Workspace applies edits, race conditions become likely.
mitigations: Run only one agent per checkout at a time.
Use separate branches for each agent.
Disable Cursor Yolo mode on shared repos.
Require a human to merge agent outputs manually.
requires-engineering: add file locks or orchestrator-level edit serialization.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot Workspace proposes edits for human review, while Cursor’s agent loop can execute multi-step tool use and shell commands. If one agent’s output is fed into the other as trusted context, mistakes can cascade into incorrect code changes or commands. The profiles do not show verification between them, so the default pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF Cursor-generated text is pasted into Copilot chat or Workspace, Copilot may treat it as authoritative context.
IF Copilot-generated edits are then executed or extended by Cursor without review, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require human review between agent handoffs.
Do not paste one agent’s raw output into the other.
Use a checklist to verify claims before acting on them.
Limit Cursor to read-only analysis when Copilot has already edited files.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agent outputs and downstream actions.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles clipboard contents and broad model-provider/MCP traffic; Copilot sends repo context to GitHub/Microsoft services under a GitHub repo OAuth scope. If the shared workspace contains regulated data, the pair can route the same data through different vendors with different retention and residency terms. The profiles do not document aligned compliance controls.
conditions: IF regulated data is present in the shared workspace, both vendors may process it.
IF the organization requires uniform retention or residency, the differing vendor paths can violate policy.
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from the shared workspace.
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings before use.
Disable clipboard sharing for sensitive projects.
Use a compliance-approved sandbox repo.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
